experimental_procedure: General/Typical Procedure: Typical Procedures for F/I exchange of secondary and tertiary alkyl fluorides. A typical procedure is given for the synthesis of 2d. To a hexane (2.5 mL) were added Et3Al (1.0 M in hexane, 0.5 mL, 0.5 mmol) and CH2I2 (80 μl, 2 mmol), then the reaction mixture was stirred for 90 min. The reaction was quenched with 3 M aqueous HCl solution slowly and extracted with hexane. The organic phase was filtered through a short pad of silica gel. experimental_procedure: General/Typical Procedure: The typical experimental procedure is as follows: p-fluorobenzotrifluoride (1.07 g, 6.5 mmol) and carbon tetrachloride (5 mL) were added to a flask with a magnetic stir bar. The flask was evacuated and backfilled with argon three times and then left under argon atmosphere. Subsequently, boron tribromide (1.95 g, 7.8 mmol) was added via a syringe. The mixture was stirred at room temperature for 36 h, slowly changing from yellow to amber in color. Then, the reaction was stopped by an addition of 15 mL of ice water. The resulting mixture was extracted with CH2Cl2 (3 x 10 mL). The combined organic layer was washed with ice water (3 x 5 mL) and dried over anhydrous CaCl2. After evaporating the solvent, the crude product was purified by flash chromatography (SiO2), and eluted with ethyl acetate/petroleum ether (Φr = 2 : 98) to give p-fluorobenzotribromide. Compound V, yield 85%. Formula: C8H4Br6; Mr: 579.54; wi(calc.)/%: C 16.58, H 0.70; wi(found)/%: C 16.60, H 0.68. M.p./°C: 195-196 (lit. 194-196). 1H NMR (CDCl3), δ: 7.21 (s, 4H, Ph) 13C NMR (CDCl3), δ: 33.77 (2C, CBr3), 126.34 (4C, Ph), 148.09 (2C, Ph) MS, m/z (Ir/%): 580 (67) (M+).

reference: Halogen Exchange Reaction of Aliphatic Fluorine Compounds with Organic Halides as Halogen Source | Mizukami, Yuki; Song, Zhiyi; Takahashi, Tamotsu | Organic Letters (2015), 17(24), 5942-5945
experimental_procedure: General/Typical Procedure: Typical procedure for F/Cl and F/Br exchange of primary alkyl fluorides. A typical procedure is given for the synthesis of 1b. To a suspension of Cp2TiCl2 (7.5 mg, 0.03 mmol) in hexane (5 mL) was added i Bu3Al (1.0 M in hexane, 1 mL, 1 mmol) dropwise at 0 ºC, and the mixture was stirred for 30 min at the same temperature, then warm up to room temperature. After the mixture was stirred for 30 min, CH2Cl2 (0.13 mL, 2 mmol) and 1-fluorooctane 1a (0.16 mL, 1 mmol) were added to the blue solution successively and stirred for 24 h. The reaction was quenched with 3 M aqueous HCl solution slowly and extracted with hexane. The organic phase was filtered through a short pad of silica gel. The solvents and volatile compounds were removed under reduced pressure. 1-Bromoadamantane (5c). The compound 5c was prepared with Cp2TiBr2 (5 mg, 0.025 mmol), Et3Al (1.0 M in hexane, 0.5 mL, 0.5 mmol), CH2Br2 (70 μL, 2 mmol) and 1-fluoroadamantane 5a (77 mg, 0.5 mmol) as colorless solid. The reaction gave a mixture of 1-bromoadamantane 5c and 1-ethyladamantane. NMR yield: 80%. CAS Registry Number [768-90-1]. 1H NMR (400 MHz, CDCl3): δ 1.72 (t, J = 2.8 Hz, 6H), 2.10 (s, 3H), 2.35 (d, J = 3.0 Hz, 6H). 13C{1H} NMR (101 MHz, CDCl3): δ 32.5, 35.5, 49.3, 66.8.

experimental_procedure: General/Typical Procedure: The typical experimental procedure is as follows: p-fluorobenzotrifluoride (1.07 g, 6.5 mmol) and carbon tetrachloride (5 mL) were added to a flask with a magnetic stir bar. The flask was evacuated and backfilled with argon three times and then left under argon atmosphere. Subsequently, boron tribromide (1.95 g, 7.8 mmol) was added via a syringe. The mixture was stirred at room temperature for 36 h, slowly changing from yellow to amber in color. Then, the reaction was stopped by an addition of 15 mL of ice water. The resulting mixture was extracted with CH2Cl2 (3 x 10 mL). The combined organic layer was washed with ice water (3 x 5 mL) and dried over anhydrous CaCl2. After evaporating the solvent, the crude product was purified by flash chromatography (SiO2), and eluted with ethyl acetate/petroleum ether (Φr = 2 : 98) to give p-fluorobenzotribromide. experimental_procedure: General/Typical Procedure: The typical experimental procedure is as follows: p-fluorobenzotrifluoride (1.07 g, 6.5 mmol) and carbon tetrachloride (5 mL) were added to a flask with a magnetic stir bar.
